prompt: The tests for my textkit package are failing. Can you fix the bugs in the package without changing tests/test_textkit.py, add a regression test for each bug you fix in tests/test_regressions.py, then run the whole suite with python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v and tell me the result?
notes: Fresh pilot task. Two independent bugs in different files make 2 of 8 tests fail: textkit/tokens.py uses rstrip('.,;:!?') so leading punctuation, quotes/brackets and punctuation-only tokens survive (docstring says strip any string.punctuation from both ends, keep inner apostrophes/hyphens); textkit/stats.py top_n sorts by count only, so ties keep first-appearance order instead of alphabetical. Pitfalls: the classic key=(count, word), reverse=True fix sorts ties reverse-alphabetically (caught by the visible test); adding only quotes/parens to the strip set passes the visible test but not the docstring; truncating before breaking ties (most_common(n) then sort) fails the tie-at-cutoff case. Checker: protected test unchanged; trusted original tests pass; hidden tokenize and word_counts/top_n probes; wordfreq.py CLI output on the trusted sample; tests/test_regressions.py has >=2 passing tests (no skips/xfails); full suite passes; red/green: the candidate's regression tests must fail (assertion failures or non-API errors, no import errors) against the original buggy package and against each half-fixed package (only the tokenize bug, only the top_n bug), built from trusted buggy/fixed copies. The final chat answer is not graded.
